did: The phone now has a Cast wing with its own launcher icon. You pick Mochi or Tin Bird and see every feeling as a live loop, six to a page, and open one to see it in each shot and corner over a sample card from a video. Every picture is drawn by the same code the videos use, and the preview piece is shared, so the signature step can reuse it. The Android build and its lint passed here before the merge.

calls.title: What the two characters' wing is called
calls.why: The epic's working name; you left the name open, so it is yours to change.
calls.undo: Change the label in the phone's wings list and the wing's words; the icon and its path stay.

calls.title: Whether the wing keeps a chosen look
options: Keep nothing; a choice lives in the page alone
Keep your last-chosen look on home now
calls.why: Nothing would read a kept look until the signature step exists.
calls.undo: Keep it with the signature step, as a call that moves this one.

calls.title: How the previews move
options: One shared clock, a 6.8 second loop at 15 pictures a second
Each preview at full rate on its own
calls.why: A page of loops redraws together and lightly on the phone, and holds still with eyes open when less motion is asked for.
calls.undo: Change the loop length or rate in the shared loop clock.

calls.title: How the wing's screens are laid out
options: A paged grid of looks, and a look page with shot and corner chips
Every look in one long scroll
calls.why: Six looks fit a phone screen, and the chips show all fifteen shot and corner pairs from one page.
calls.undo: Change the page size or the defaults in the wing's model and words.

left: Every look shows its character's resting loop until HOST3 and HOST4 fill in the emotion loops; the wing needs no change when they do.
Themes and costumes (HOST7) are not in the wing yet, because their sets don't exist; when they do, the look page gets chips for them and the words table their names.
Each video's beats in the wing (HOST10) is its own story, not started.

For the signature (HOST16): import HostPreview and useLoopTime from the shared UI package. HostPreview takes beats, a seed, a time or 'still', an aspect and what the host stands over. useLoopTime wraps every 6.8 seconds, so a scene longer than that drives the time from the signature's own playhead and keeps 'still' for reduced motion.
The wing reaches the phone with the next approved release of the app.
